compatibleChanges.rationale: Retains the additive optional commandId plus device-pairing and command-receipt request variants while sharing the existing attachment declarations with canonical timeline payloads. Existing request fields and variants remain unchanged; older daemons continue parsing old requests and reject only newly invoked RPC variants they do not implement. The compaction timeline item additionally gains optional outcome and error fields; its status enum stays loading|completed, so an older app parses every terminal compaction exactly as before and simply ignores the refinement. Daseo adds the agent.side_question.request variant (/btw side questions); a new request type that older daemons reject as unknown, and newer clients send it only when server_info.features.sideQuestion is true. Daseo browser automation (deltas 26 and 28) changes the browser.automation.execute.response and hello capability shapes the app sends to the daemon. Tab info gains an optional loadingForMs; an older daemon's non-strict object schema strips it and parses the list_tabs reply as before. The result union gains a network variant (browser_network capture: action, capturing, optional entries with seq/method/url/resourceType/status/mimeType/failed/startedAt/durationMs/requestHeaders/bodies, optional cursor/hasMore/pendingCount/droppedCount). An older daemon would reject that unknown result command, so compatibility rests on never sending it: the app returns a network result only in reply to a network request, which an older daemon has no tool to issue. A newer app advertises network in browserHost.supportedCommands, and an older daemon's capability parser drops unknown command names (checked: ["snapshot","future_cmd"] parses to ["snapshot"]).

Retains the additive optional turnOutcome, feature flags, device-pairing, push-catch-up, and command-receipt responses, and adds optional imageCount and attachments to canonical user timeline rows. Existing response fields and variants remain unchanged; older clients ignore optional object fields and never receive new RPC responses unless they send the corresponding new request. The compaction timeline item additionally gains optional outcome and error fields; its status enum stays loading|completed, so an older app parses every terminal compaction exactly as before and simply ignores the refinement. The compaction timeline item also gains an optional turnId (Daseo 6ef0fdbb1) that older apps ignore. Canonical user timeline rows additionally gain one optional origin field ("system") marking Paseo system prompts; all existing fields and variants remain unchanged, and an older app ignores the optional field and renders the row as a plain user message. Daseo adds the agent.side_question.response variant, sent only in reply to agent.side_question.request, and the optional server_info.features.sideQuestion flag that older apps ignore. Daseo browser automation (delta 28) adds a network variant to the browser.automation.execute.request command union (action start|stop|list; optional urlIncludes, method, resourceType, since; primitive defaults for maxEntries, includeBodies, includeRequestBodies). An older app's generated outbound validator rejects an unknown command: the client logs "Message validation failed" and drops that one message (checked against the generated validator), so the variant is not tolerated as unknown data. Compatibility rests on the capability gate instead: the broker sends a command only to a host whose browserHost.supportedCommands includes it (unsupportedCommandFailure runs before sendRequest), older apps derive that list from their own command names and never advertise network, so they get no request and the agent receives browser_unsupported. Existing command and result variants are unchanged; the iframe snapshot work (delta 27) changes no wire schema.
Adds one optional E2EE v2 metadata object while retaining v:2, serverId, daemonPublicKeyB64, and relay unchanged, so older clients parse the same offer and use the legacy authenticated channel.
